projects.title: Approval cutoff for a consumer lender
projects.result: +$7.1M realized NPV from a new approval cutoff, at the same bad rate
projects.what: realized NPV from a new approval cutoff, at the same bad rate
projects.question: Can a new approval cutoff increase approvals at the same bad rate?
projects.answer: Yes. A scorecard cutoff approves more applicants at the same bad rate and adds $7.1M of realized NPV on the 2015 loans.

keyline.h: It approves more applicants with no more defaults
keyline.p: Approval rate: 85.7% vs. 84.5% today. Bad rate (default rate of approved loans): 12.5%, held equal.

keyline.h: The gain holds under every cost assumption tested
keyline.p: Realized NPV against the current policy: +$7.1M. Lowest result in the stress test: +$5.1M.

keyline.h: A small test limits the risk of the change
keyline.p: Start on 10% of applications. Stop if 12-month defaults rise 1 point.

projects.title: Transaction policy for card fraud
projects.result: $64k lower monthly cost of fraud, false declines and reviews
projects.what: lower total cost of fraud, false declines and reviews
projects.question: Which policy gives the lowest total cost of fraud, false declines and reviews?
projects.answer: The lowest-cost policy cuts the total monthly cost by $64k and keeps false declines under the 3% cap.

keyline.h: It lowers the cost that matters, not only fraud loss
keyline.p: Total monthly cost = fraud loss that gets through + cost of false declines + cost of reviews. Decrease: $64,274 per month.

keyline.h: The saving is the low end of the estimate
keyline.p: The decrease is $64k to $127k per month, depending on the baseline. I report the lowest figure.
False decline rate (share of good transactions declined): 2.46%, under the cap of 3%.

projects.title: Offer targeting for an email campaign
projects.result: $13k profit per campaign from an email to all customers, with no targeting model
projects.what: profit from an email to all customers, with no targeting model
projects.question: Which customers do we send the offer to, for the best return?
projects.answer: Send the men's email to all customers and keep a 10% holdout. It earns $13k per campaign of 100,000 customers.

keyline.p: Spend effect against the no-email group: +$0.77 per customer in the 2 weeks after the email.

keyline.h: The extra margin is larger than the contact cost
keyline.p: 30% margin on $0.77, less $0.10 for each email, gives $13,095 of profit per 100,000 customers.

keyline.h: A targeting model adds nothing at this cost
keyline.p: At $0.10 per email, no model-picked segment earns more than an email to all customers.
